title: Noninvasive Assessment of Intracranial Pressure Using Otoacoustic Emissions in Healthy Subjects and Glaucoma Patients
official: Noninvasive Intracranial Pressure Assessment Using Otoacoustic Emissions in Healthy Subjects and Glaucoma Patients
summary:
The COSMO study aims to investigate whether a noninvasive test based on otoacoustic emissions, which are sounds produced by the inner ear, can provide useful information about changes in intracranial pressure in people with glaucoma and healthy individuals.

Glaucoma is an eye disease that can damage the optic nerve and cause vision loss. Researchers believe that the relationship between pressure inside the eye and pressure inside the skull may play a role in glaucoma.

This study will compare measurements of distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) between patients with glaucoma and healthy participants. Researchers will assess how reproducible these measurements are and how they change with different body positions and changes in intraocular pressure.

Participants will undergo eye examinations and noninvasive ear measurements while assuming different body positions.

The results may help researchers better understand the relationship between intracranial pressure, intraocular pressure, and glaucoma, and evaluate the potential usefulness of otoacoustic emissions as a noninvasive assessment method.
criteria:
\*\*Inclusion Criteria:\*\*

General inclusion criteria (all participants):

* Age between 50 and 70 years.
* Central corneal thickness between 500 and 600 µm.
* Patent ear canal at otoscopy.
* Written informed consent freely provided before the start of any study procedures.
* Ability to understand and willingness to follow study instructions and likely to complete all required study visits and procedures.

Additional inclusion criteria for healthy subjects:

* No eye disease.
* No family history of glaucoma.

Additional inclusion criteria for glaucoma patients:

* Clinical diagnosis of primary open-angle glaucoma, normal-tension glaucoma, pseudoexfoliative glaucoma, or pigmentary glaucoma.
* Reproducible visual field defect on the Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA) 24-2 test compatible with glaucoma, defined by the presence of a cluster of three or more non-continuous points in the pattern deviation plot with a probability of occurrence in the normal population of less than 5%, including at least one point with p \< 1%, a pattern standard deviation with p \< 5%, or a Glaucoma Hemifield Test result outside normal limits.
* Optic nerve head (ONH) abnormalities compatible with glaucoma, including generalized or focal enlargement of the optic cup, thinning of the neuroretinal rim, cup-to-disc ratio asymmetry greater than 0.2 between eyes, or retinal nerve fiber layer loss.

\*\*Exclusion Criteria:\*\*

General exclusion criteria (all participants):

* History of inner or middle ear disease.
* History of cerebral diseases that may increase intracranial pressure (ICP), including neoplastic, ischemic, toxic, or infectious causes of cerebral edema, hydrocephalus, obstruction of major venous sinuses, vascular malformations, or idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
* Systemic treatment with medications known to affect ICP, including corticosteroids, nitroprusside, nitroglycerin, hydralazine, nicardipine, topiramate, and loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide).
* Non-recordable distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs).
* Uncontrolled blood pressure, with or without systemic treatment.
* Retinal or optic nerve head diseases other than glaucoma, as assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans of the macula, optic nerve head, and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL).
* Phacoemulsification or glaucoma filtering surgery within the previous 6 months.

Additional exclusion criterion for healthy subjects:

\- Intraocular pressure (IOP) greater than 21 mmHg.

Additional exclusion criterion for glaucoma patients:

\- Oral acetazolamide treatment as part of the therapeutic regimen, due to its potential effect on intracranial pressure.
